title: Timeboxed instrumentation sprint charter and metrics contract
content:
Purpose:
- Define a 2-week, timeboxed instrumentation sprint model focused on high-impact metrics, pragmatic tracing changes, and a small set of dashboard edits so we can reduce observability debt without blocking feature work.
- Produce a lightweight metrics contract for each changed signal so consumers (SRE, runtime, product) have clear semantics and acceptance criteria.

Sprint rhythm and scope (timeboxed):
- Duration: 10 working days (Mon-Fri x2)
- Pod model: 2 pods of 3 engineers + 1 product/ops liasion each (one runtime-heavy, one dashboard/alert-heavy)
- Goal: ship 5 metric contracts + tracing sampling experiment + 3 dashboard widgets trimmed or added

Priority signal list (initial):
1) inference/request-latency-ms (p50/p95/p99) - derive from span end - high priority
2) kv-cache-hit-rate - per-tenant, 5m rollup - critical for cost SLOs
3) batching-efficacy (tokens-per-batch median) - approximate from batcher events
4) model-fallback-rate - counts of fallback_invocations by reason
5) external-downstream-error-rate - 5xx from third-party routing

Metrics contract template (required for each signal):
- name
- owner
- definition (exact event or span, tags/labels)
- aggregation window and granularity
- units and desired SLI thresholds (example: p95 < 120ms for hosted tier)
- retention/rollup policy
- instrumentation PR link and rollout playbook
- consumer list (dashboards/alerts / product teams)

Tracing changes & experiments:
- Add a low-overhead span at router:router-decision with tag model_variant to correlate routing hotpaths.
- Try 3 sampling strategies in parallel (A/B):
  A) uniform 0.5% global
  B) severity-weighted (error traces 100%, latency outliers 5%)
  C) tenant-priority (top-10 tenants 10% else 0.1%)
- Shadow mode for 48h: trace writes captured but not used for alerts; validate costs.
- Acceptance: sampling config that keeps trace QPS cost delta < 12% while preserving >90% of useful investigative traces per incident replay test.

Dashboard plan (quick wins):
- Trim panels: remove duplicate p95 panels for same flow (consolidate per-route).
- Add a golden-path widget: user perceived latency (frontend-synth + backend p50) for quick SLA checks.
- Add KV cache heatmap (tenant x time) to detect cold-start tenants.
- Widget owners assigned; each widget has one-line query and a fallback visualization if query times out.

Rollout & verification checklist (per metric/trace change):
- Instrumentation PR open and linked
- Unit tests for metric tags + acceptance test that synthetic events surface metric
- Canary: enable for dev then staging then 10% prod for 24h
- Validation queries and stored baseline results (commit to PR)
- Alert sensitivity test (simulate spike, verify alert triggers & noise)
- Post-rollout retro note in thread with cost delta and any consumer feedback

Acceptance criteria (definition of done):
- Metric contract completed and reviewed by at least one downstream consumer
- Dashboard widgets created/edited and smoke-checked by owner
- Tracing config applied in shadow and validated against replay cases
- Linked PRs merged + rollout runbook published in Confluence

Risks and constraints:
- Trace storage costs can spike; keep shadow-mode and cost cap enforced by infra budget guardrail
- Tenant-level high-cardinality tags: restrict tag cardinality (max 3 dynamic values per metric)
- Query cost on dashboards: limit panels to 60s queries and use rollups where possible

Open questions / parking lot:
- Do we standardize p99 latency alerts across tiers or keep per-product thresholds? (action: product apiece decision)
- Who owns retention tiers beyond 90 days for high-cardinality debug traces?
- Should we add an operator-facing compact dashboard with 3x key SLI tiles for oncall?

Immediate next steps (this doc owner):
- Kickoff meeting Fri 2025-02-14 10:00 (calendar invite out) - align owners and pod assignments
- Create PR template for metric contract (Jun)
- Instrument router-decision span prototype (Marcus)
- Dashboard trim list and baseline queries (Priya)

Quick links and references:
- Baseline telemetry decisions: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/12345
- Current alert registry: OBS-4123
- Tracing RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/198
- Slack kickoff thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0ABC1/thread/11111

Notes to self (working draft style):
- Keep narrative short in PRs; reviewers get flooded.
- If a metric touches billing/cost signals, loop in finance early.
- Prototype sampling on a small tenant set first to measure storage delta.

Status: draft — expect several iterations after kickoff and first canary.
